newsitem.title: UK: Eurostocks, dollar fall as Wall St rally fails.
newsitem.headline: Eurostocks, dollar fall as Wall St rally fails.

text.p: European equity markets fell back to the morning's lows on Wednesday afternoon as Wall Street failed to sustain an opening rally despite key U.S. economic data which virtually removed all fears of a near term rise in U.S. interest rates.

A downturn in U.S. stock index futures and the failure of the bond market to capitalise on the benign inflation data undercut the early U.S. rally, which saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average rise to 8040.51 points, up 79.67. By 1429 GMT, it had fallen back 68.29 points to 7892.34.
The dollar also slid back against the mark after finding support early afternoon on U.S. data, showing yet another fall in factory gate prices and higher retail sales.
The greenback remained pressured by the possibility that the Bundesbank might raise interest rates to combat higher German inflation.
The U.S. Labour Department said its July producer price index fell 0.1 percent, while the Commerce Department said July retail sales rose 0.6 percent.
Fears that inflationary pressures were building up in the American economy were behind Tuesday's sharp fall on Wall Street which dragged European stock markets lower this morning.
But the seventh fall in a row in the monthly producer price index cheered markets on both sides of the Atlantic, which had been expecting a rise of 0.1 percent.

"We have had seven consecutive months...of declines in the producer price index. This is unprecedented in U.S. economic history," said Thomas Carpenter, chief economist and managing director at A.S.B. Capital in the U.S.
"What this means is that from the (Federal Reserve) standpoint it is virtually impossible to increase the level of Fed funds on August 19," Carpenter added.
The Federal Reserve Bank is due to meet to consider whether to adjust interest rates on August 19.
In London, the FTSE-100 index of leading shares, which was initially pulled higher by the firmer Wall Street opening, fell back to 4,996.8 points, down 79.0, or 1.56 percent.

London's morning decline was partly influenced by the potentially inflationary impact of a greater than expected fall in U.K. unemployment. Official figures showed that 5.5 percent of the workforce was unemployed in July, down from 5.7 percent in June, a larger fall than the market had bargained for.
However, U.K. interest rates London are unlikely to rise again soon. A Bank of England report signalled that monetary policy may stay on hold after four successive monthly rate rises.
Bank of England Deputy Governor Mervyn King also said that the period of stability now possible in U.K. monetary policy may not be followed by an increase in interest rates.
These remarks helped drive sterling to its lowest level for a month at 2.90 marks.
Paris also took its cue from U.S. stocks, moving off the lows when Wall Street opened, only to fall back later. The CAC-40 index was 71.82 points, or 2.37 percent down at 2927.65 by 1435 GMT.
The tone in Frankfurt was gloomier than in London and Paris as traders were unsettled by the talk of an imminent rise in German interest rates.
The IBIS DAX index was 2.97 percent lower at 4247.56 points, down 128.93 by 1436 GMT in computerised trading after the close of floor trade on the bourse.
The dollar's weakness stemmed from a hawkish assessment on German inflation by the Bundesbank, traders said.

In its August monthly report, published early on Wednesday, the Bundesbank said it could not overlook a stronger rise in consumer prices in the last few months, and would shape its policy in such a way that price stability can be maintained.
On Tuesday, data for July showed that German inflation rose to 1.9 percent, the highest level since June 1995 and up from 1.7 percent in June.

"The assertion that the exchange rate is very significant in policy decisions, the fact that they highlight the recent rise in some inflation figures and the desire to see M3 growth lower, suggest they may be closer to a rate increase than previously thought," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.

Even though the CPI data was boosted by one-off factors last month, economists expect it to rise above 2.0 percent soon, the level regarded as acceptable by the Bundesbank. German import prices, due to be released later this month, are also key for signs whether the weakness of the mark is boosting inflation.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted around 1.8320/25 marks and 115.49/54 yen, compared with 1.8665 and 115.78 in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1440 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 79.2 points at 4,996.6.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was down 84.61 points at 4278.48.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was down 61.67 at 2935.90.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was $2.40 an ounce weaker in London at $326.20. Silver was one cent down at $4.46.
